canonical565_outcome_preserved.reason: For the direct replication of Liberman and Trope (1998, Study 1) on the 19-item BIF (omitting the original free-writing task and administering the 6 excluded BIF items on a separate page), the authors evaluated the replication against two explicit preregistered criteria—consistency in direction and consistency in magnitude—within an overall 'limited support' synthesis. They explicitly conclude that the temporal-distance replication effect was consistent in direction (d = 0.08, 95% CI [0.003, 0.16]; d = 0.12, 95% CI [0.06, 0.19] after valence adjustment) but inconsistent in magnitude with the original effect (d = 0.92, only 9% of the original size, with the replication CI upper bound excluding 0.92). Moreover, excluding the 21.5% comprehension-check failures caused the 95% CI to include zero (d = 0.08, 95% CI [-0.004, 0.17]), and item-level analyses showed 5 of 19 BIF items with CIs excluding zero in the predicted direction versus 5 of 19 in the opposite direction. Under the codebook, because the authors themselves present the Liberman & Trope (1998, Study 1) evidence as partly supporting (direction) and partly not supporting (magnitude and robustness) rather than as an unqualified success or the social-distance failure quoted in the shipped row, the outcome is 'mixed'.
